synopsis: The corpus distinguishes tools built for or deliberately adapted to off-road working machines from predominantly road-origin simulation platforms, noting that quarry environments lack lanes, curbs and traffic lights [f16072, f16073]. Relevant options include mobile-machinery physics tools, road-validation platforms with explicit off-road packages, and procedural scene generators with examples across agriculture, forestry and construction [f16074, f16075, f4194]. Concrete milestones include Foretellix’s 2021 mines-and-quarries partnership, MineSim’s April 2025 open-pit truck benchmark, Applied Intuition–Komatsu’s 9 September 2025 partnership covering staffed-site collision avoidance, and MathWorks R2026b excavator, backhoe and haul-truck examples [f9184, f16083, f8399, f8379]. Scene-creation examples include Agri-Sim reported in August 2026 and AgriGen on Isaac Sim reported in September 2026; MineSim draws on two real mines and models unstructured roads and truck response lag, but is treated as evidence of closed-loop scenario feasibility rather than validated sensor physics [f4147, f4142, f16084, f16092]. For planning, off-road relevance should not be equated with braking validation: only a few suppliers publicly position for construction or mining sensing, most capabilities remain claims rather than independently demonstrated results, and independent automatic-braking validation for any listed tool, dataset or framework was not found [f8284, f16091].
